recipes.name: Apricot Chicken with Balsamic Vinegar
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds chicken breast tenderloins, cut into bite-size pieces
0.25 cup balsamic vinegar, or to taste

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet with a lid over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper, and cook in the hot oil until golden brown around the edges, but still pink in the center, about 5 minutes. Stir in the onion, and cook for about 3 minutes more. Pour in the balsamic vinegar, bring it to a simmer, and allow it to reduce for a few minutes.

Cut half of the apricots in half, leaving the others whole. Place the apricots into the skillet, and pour in the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, then stir in the apricot preserves and thyme. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the apricots have softened, 10 to 15 minutes. Sprinkle with chopped parsley to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Apricot Chicken with Balsamic Vinegar
raw_recipe.description: This chicken is cooked with apricots, balsamic vinegar, broth, and thyme. It's super yummy and a hit every time!

review.reviewBody: 4.5 stars actually. This recipe was quick to prepare and turned out well. Instead of apricot preserves, I used apricot "simply fruit" which may have been a little less sweet...it had the right amount of sweetness in the end. I also used canned apricots instead of dried which were juicier and may have made a little more sauce than originally intended. I added just a little cornstarch to thicken the sauce and served it with orzo pilaf and broccoli. Make sure to serve this with rice or pasta to go along with all of the sauce.

This recipe was not very good in my humble opinion. I thought it was too sweet even though I cut the jam in half and used jam for diabetics (no added sugar). I also felt something was missing from the recipe. The chicken cut into pieces was also a bit much. I think if the chicken breasts were left whole, browned, and then braised in the sauce, it might be better both flavor and presentation-wise. I wonder if it would be better with added sliced carrots and/or red bell pepper, while cutting down on the amount of dried apricots. I also wonder if adding some cumin, cayenne, and maybe a small amount of cinnamon might give the sauce a warmer, more complex profile to balance the sweetness.

With a few tweaks, this recipe came out great! To reduce the sweetness of the original recipe, I added a little dijon mustard into the balsamic vinegar and upped the amount of vinegar to 1/3 cup. I also reduced the amount of jam to 1/2 cup. Yummy!

Pretty good as written, but I left out the optional onions. I'm glad, because they had no business in this recipe. Needed a little something, so the second time I added some cayenne pepper, used skinless bone-in chicken, and baked in the oven @ 350, basting occasionally. Cover with foil to keep the sauce from burning. My hubby likes to buy different kinds of balsamic vinegar, so I used some that had figs in it. That was awesome.

I made the recipe as written but used sugar free apricot preserves and a tbsp of dried thyme instead of fresh thyme. The reviews suggested thickening the broth so I decided to add 4 fresh carrots cut in chunks and I prepared a package of black beans and rice which I added to the chicken to create a complete meal. Outstanding flavors! Thank you for sharing this recipe.

I made this dish for my husband who is very picky--- he loves complex flavors. This dish was very easy to make. I did two things differently-- I added more fresh apricots, all sliced in halves. In order to cut down on the sweetness I used only a very large dollop of preserves as opposed to a full cup and I added 5 cloves, the cloves chopped in large pieces. I also let the liquid reduce to an almost glaze-like finish. Was fab! Over rice pilaf, served w/ French cut green beans and this was a hit.

This was excellent! I followed other reviews and cut the preserve in half. Glad I did (only because I am not big on sweetness), I used fresh sage as I had no thyme on hand. And right before serving, I added a bit of flour and water to thicken sauce just a little. I think this recipe really calls for your own personal touch. People that like sweetness could add more preserve or even add a touch of balsamic reduction for those that dont. Great recipe!

I know, I know, I didn’t make this exactly as written, but I got as close as I could. I used canned chopped peaches and peach preserves. And I cut back on the preserves a bit because I didn’t want it to be too sweet. My version was quite good, as I’m sure it would have been using the apricots. Since my peaches didn’t need to soften, I put them in last just to warm them through, setting some aside for garnish, along with a garnish of fresh thyme instead of the parsley. I served this over Brazilian White Rice, also from this site. We both enjoyed this dinner!

Complete yes! I did reduce the apricot jam to about 1/3 of a cup and I wouldn't have wanted it sweeter than that. I loved the taste and texture of the dried apricots and they really added something to the dish. There was probably too much chicken broth because it was still swimming in sauce, so maybe I'd only use 1/2 cup next time. It would still cook the chicken but be less "soupy".

I made this recipe this evening and it was delish. Served it with the large pearl couscous. I did not have dried apricots so I used fresh ones instead and no preserves. In addition to the balsamic vinegar, added some fig vinegar for a bit more fruity flavor. I also finished it with a 1/4 cup of heavy cream added at the end.

Easy to make and yummy flavor, but I agree with other reviewers; it is much too sweet so apricot preserves in half (at least) and I also think half as many dried apricots would have been plenty. I also brined the chicken for an hour in the fridge before cooking, to keep it moist.
Very good, its a keeper. Family loved it.

I read the reviews and added 10 apricots and 1/4 cup preserves I also added a little Dijon mustard. This was a good recipe. My family liked it but did not rave about it. I may make again in the future Thank you for the recipe

Love this and so does the boyfriend, so its a win for us! I do add an extra splash of balsalmic, but make it as written otherwise. Served over rice with the sauce is heavenly. Definitely a quick, straightforward staple.
Used peaches instead of apricots
Love this recipe. Will definitely make it again.
This was delicious. I used apricot preserves instead of fresh apricot .
Very tasty but had way too much liquid at the end of the cooking time. Added a Tbs of corn starch to thicken a bit
A bit too sweet for me, and not all that tasty. I did add a little more balsamic after what i read in these reviews, but sadly, it just wasnt that good.

This was great and I would definitely make it again. The flavor is very, very rich, so it is best with mild sides, like plain rice. It was a little watery, which is my only real negative. Everyone at dinner enjoyed it a lot.
